sources.title: Redisson RedissonLock source (commit e40b177, checked date)
Redisson LockPubSub source (commit e40b177, checked date)

claims.text: At Redisson commit e40b177, RedissonLock is documented as non-fair. Its blocking tryLock first attempts tryAcquire, subtracts elapsed time from total waitTime, subscribes only while remaining budget is positive, subtracts subscription time, retries in a loop, waits on an entry latch for the applicable TTL or remaining wait time, and unsubscribes in finally when the flow ends.

At Redisson commit e40b177, RedissonLock's unlock script returns without release for a non-owner, decrements the reentrancy counter and retains/extends the lock while the counter remains positive, and only deletes the lock then publishes LockPubSub.UNLOCK_MESSAGE on final release. LockPubSub.onMessage releases the entry latch for that message; a released latch is followed by another acquisition attempt in RedissonLock rather than direct lock ownership transfer.

At Redisson commit e40b177, an unsuccessful acquisition waits on the local latch for TTL when TTL is shorter than remaining wait time, otherwise for remaining wait time, then retries; this time-based path is independent of a received unlock latch release.

Redis official distributed-lock documentation describes SET with NX and PX for a single-instance lock, a unique random lock value, and conditional release so a client does not delete a lock acquired later by another client; it explains the lease validity-time boundary.
